Preflight Demo Program
DOC-0009 2026-06-08
Desk Vocabulary for Issues and Priority Requests
Compiled: 2026-06-08
Compiler: Demo Worker 0036, Demo Team 06
Use: Wording aid for fictional queue correspondence.
ISSUE TERMS
open — An issue status value. Use it for that exact value, not as a loose
replacement for every issue still requiring queue attention.
in_progress — An issue status value indicating progress within the tracking
workflow. Keep the underscore when writing a field value. The same spelling
also occurs in the task vocabulary, so name the record type.
blocked — An issue status value for the blocked category. Under the record
contract, an issue in this category has an unfinished associated task. A paper
routing delay alone does not establish the category.
reopened — An issue status value supported by a closure event followed by a
reopening event. Its current closure timestamp is empty. A renewed
conversation does not itself establish that history.
closed — An issue status value with a populated closure timestamp. It
describes the issue record, not the completion of every conversation that may
mention it.
unresolved — A collective query term for issue statuses other than closed. It
includes open, in_progress, blocked, and reopened. Writers must say whether
they mean this collective term or the exact open category.
PRIORITY WORDS
low, medium, high — The exact permitted priority labels, in increasing order
of queue priority. They are separate from status. In a request, put a proposed
value under proposal and a reason under justification. Never infer priority
from the darkness of handwriting or an envelope's position.
TASK WORDS
D. Worker 0036
Demo Worker 0036, Demo Team 06

pages.text:
Preflight Demo Program
DOC-0009 2026-06-08
todo, in_progress, awaiting_review, completed, blocked — Task statuses. The
awaiting _review category has an empty completion timestamp; completed
has a populated one. Task completion does not automatically close an issue.
review, investigation, documentation, inspection, rectification — Task kind
labels used to organize tracking entries. Here they identify categories only.
They provide no directions for physical activity.
SUBSYSTEM WORDS
hydraulics, avionics, electrical, cabin, structures, controls — Exact grouping
labels on issue records. Copy their spelling when identifying a filter; do not
turn a subsystem label into a team name.
REFERENCE USE
ISSUE-0101, DEMO-AIR-0007, and TASK-0969 may serve as locating
references in a correspondence question. Their appearance on this vocabulary
sheet supplies no record values. Ask the records for such values when a
discussion needs them.
Editorial note: Keep the record type beside ambiguous terms. This sheet
defines vocabulary, not a snapshot of the queue.
D. Worker 0036
Demo Worker 0036, Demo Team 06
